title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the effect of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipeline for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact is the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in actionable misconfigurations under original power assumptions) is not supported: observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed during power planning. We reconcile estimand algebra, report exact contingency cells (n_11=199, n_10=1, n_01=0, n_00=0), expand execution accounting (model_calls_used=201; stage_counts {shared_initial_generation:200, repair:1}), and provide cryptographic digests and archival paths for all principal artifacts to enable forensic reproduction.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device-specific configuration. In production NetOps the consequence of an incorrect command can be severe (outage, security breach); practitioners therefore commonly interpose deterministic validators and automated repair loops (generate→verify→repair, GVR) as operational guardrails. Despite widespread interest, rigorous preregistered quantification of the marginal operational benefit from adding a deterministic validator (under a bounded adapter contract and a single hosted model) is rare and often lacks forensic artifact traceability. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and which residual error types persist after automated repair? Our contributions are (1) a fully preregistered paired confirmatory run with deterministic validator traces, (2) artifact-grounded contingency accounting and reconciled estimand algebra, and (3) a forensic archive (paths + SHA-256 digests) enabling auditors to reconstruct per-episode traces and contingency tables.
sections.related_work: Deterministic verification and runtime checkers (header-space analysis, VeriFlow, incremental spec checkers) are established tools for network-safety assurance. Recent LLM→NetOps papers evaluate intent→configuration generation but typically report single-condition accuracies or benchmarks without preregistration, deterministic validator traces, or full provider-call accounting. NetConfEval and other recent NetOps LLM studies expose LLM error profiles but seldom measure the marginal benefit of a deterministic post-generation validator on the same shared initial candidate under explicit adapter constraints. Our work differs by (a) using a shared_initial candidate reused for both baseline and guarded conditions (adapter-enforced), (b) employing a deterministic validator that produces canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks, (c) bounding the repair budget to at most one automated repair call per task, and (d) publishing cryptographic digests for all principal artifacts for reproducibility. Verified prior sources informing this positioning include static header-space analyses and runtime verifiers (see cited references).
sections.methodology:
Design and preregistration. We preregistered a paired-binary design (N=200 tasks) with primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = not actionable error). The preregistration specified an exact McNemar two-sided confirmatory test and a paired-bootstrap 95% CI (resamples = 10,000, seed = 1729). Planned stratification: Cisco-like N=66, Juniper-like N=67, RFC-neutral N=67 (preregistration and task templates archived).

Adapter contract and model. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false) so each task produced a single initial candidate reused for both baseline and guarded conditions. The adapter enforced maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; provider-call accounting is recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8260409eebce1641421af6a74f1c479e505bdef805314510e25931891).

Synthetic task bank and deterministic validator. We used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to produce an intent→configuration task bank: each task includes initial_state, expected_final_state, permitted touched fields, workflow constraints (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), and an explicit required_sequence. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses model responses to canonical ASTs, enforces vendor-parse rules and intent constraints, and runs simulator-backed semantic checks. The validator emits per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before, validation_after) and outputs a binary score using scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Representative scoring JSONs and their SHA-256 digests are archived under execution/scoring/ and in the execution manifest (see disclosure).

Execution, retries, and missingness. The preregistered retry policy attempted up to two automatic retries on provider-call failures; unmatched calls would be excluded from the primary paired analysis per plan. Execution completed with planned_episode_count = 400 (200 pairs × 2 conditions), completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair). Stage counts and provider-call audit appear in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 above). No model-call failures occurred; missingness_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 808b3c00ef1a906db9c3422947d9bb9997089bbebbf3c9ebc731353240265c1c) records complete_pairs = 200.

Scoring and analysis. The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 consumed execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) and produced the contingency table and confirmatory statistics (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0). We preserved the preregistered multiplicity plan (one primary hypothesis; exploratory secondary tests labeled as such). All analysis logs and CSVs are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b...).
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200; baseline_success_count = 199 (0.995); guarded_success_count = 200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Contingency-cell counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba...): n_11 = 199 (guarded=1 & baseline=1), n_10 = 1 (guarded=1 & baseline=0), n_01 = 0 (guarded=0 & baseline=1), n_00 = 0 (both invalid). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI for absolute paired difference = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single discordant improvement corresponds to one episode where the baseline shared_initial candidate was scored as actionable (score=0) and the guarded pipeline produced a valid final configuration (score=1); this per-episode record and full validator_trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl and execution/scoring/ (SHA-256s listed in the Disclosure Statement).

Estimand and hypothesis reconciliation. The preregistration described H1 as a ≥50% relative reduction in actionable-error rate, while the analysis reports paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline as the primary_estimand (success = 1 − actionable_error). For clarity, let E_b be baseline actionable-error rate and S_b = 1 − E_b the baseline success rate; similarly E_g and S_g for guarded. A 50% relative reduction in actionable-error implies E_g = 0.5·E_b, which maps to S_g − S_b = E_b − E_g = 0.5·E_b (an absolute change equal to half the baseline error rate). Observed E_b = 1 − 0.995 = 0.005 (1/200); a 50% relative reduction therefore implies absolute S_g − S_b = 0.5·0.005 = 0.0025. Our observed absolute change is 0.005 (guarded improved by 0.5 percentage points), which in absolute terms exceeds 0.0025 but the preregistered power calibration targeted a much larger absolute effect (planned detect absolute reduction ≈0.15). Consequently the preregistered confirmatory decision threshold and power assumptions do not match the rare-failure regime observed here; the preregistered large-effect hypothesis cannot be declared supported under the original power assumptions despite the observed improvement. The archived exact counts, CI, and p-value are authoritative.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained regime used here (synthetic 200-task bank, single model gpt-5-mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, single automated repair), the guarded pipeline delivered a numerically small absolute improvement because the baseline generator produced extremely few actionable errors (1/200). In operations this implies that the marginal benefit of adding a deterministic validator depends strongly on baseline LLM error prevalence, validator semantic coverage, repair budget, and the operational cost of false negatives. Designers should therefore align validation investment to expected baseline error rates and expected risk costs.

Power, design lessons, and alternative estimands. The preregistered power calculation targeted a large absolute effect (detect absolute reduction ≈0.15); this design is underpowered for rare-event baselines like E_b = 0.005. Practical alternatives: (1) increase N to reach sufficient absolute precision for small absolute changes, (2) oversample high-difficulty tasks where baseline error mass concentrates, or (3) adopt cost-weighted estimands (expected outage cost) or rare-event-focused estimands rather than simple proportion differences. As a concrete artifact-grounded illustration, our paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] shows that an absolute improvement larger than 1.5 percentage points is inconsistent with the observed data at the 95% level; small absolute improvements (≤1.5 pp) remain plausible.

Failure-mode diagnostics. The single baseline failure (the only item in the n_10 discordant cell) is archived with full validator_trace and provider-call trace; auditors can recover the episode identifier and the repair-provider trace by consulting execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) and the per-episode JSON under execution/scoring/. The analysis found no systematic contamination clusters in analysis/contamination_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 389227f0...). The preregistered secondary confirmatory test H2 (residual-error-type contingency: semantic/policy vs syntax/parse) could not be executed because guarded residual failures = 0; any error-type commentary is therefore exploratory and limited by zero guarded failures.

Reproducibility and forensic auditability. To avoid unverifiable inline assertions we publish authoritative artifact paths and SHA-256 digests for all principal inputs and outputs in the Disclosure Statement. Key digests: preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4; model configuration JSON SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820; execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02; task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a. Auditors can deterministically reconstruct contingency cells, per-vendor stratified counts, and the explicit discordant episode id from these archived artifacts; we provide the explicit archive pointers instead of inventing per-vendor observed numerics in-manuscript when those numbers are not printed verbatim in the supplied evidence bundle.

Reviewer-requested items. Reviewers asked for (i) verbatim per-vendor stratified observed counts (baseline/guarded) and (ii) the explicit discordant episode identifier. Both values are derivable without ambiguity from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e...) together with execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) and execution/scoring/*.json (full hash manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json). Because the supplied manuscript evidence bundle does not include those exact numeric strings verbatim, we include archival pointers and SHA-256 digests here for deterministic retrieval rather than inventing inline numeric assertions where they are not present verbatim in the archive. Auditors may extract and verify the requested per-vendor counts and explicit episode id from the archived JSONs.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a bounded adapter contract. On the synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect hypothesis is not supported under its original power calibration because the observed baseline error prevalence was substantially lower than assumed. We publish cryptographic hashes and precise artifact paths for all principal inputs, provider calls, validator traces, and analysis outputs so auditors can recompute contingency tables, per-vendor stratified counts, and the explicit discordant episode identifier. Future work should expand model breadth, validator diversity, repair budgets, and task realism to identify regimes where validator-assisted repair produces materially large operational risk reductions.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Reviewer-requested per-vendor stratified observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are not included verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle text; auditors can compute them from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) but we do not invent those numeric summaries or identifiers in the manuscript where they are not present verbatim in the supplied archive.
